title: Choose Boring Technology
excerpt: Probably the single best thing to happen to me in my career was having had Kellan placed in charge of me. I stuck around long enough to see Kellan’s technical decisionmaking start to bear fruit. I learned a great deal from this, but I also learned a great deal as a result of this. I would not have been free to become the engineer that wrote Data Driven Products Now! if Kellan had not been there to so thoroughly stick the landing on technology choices.
content_html:
Probably the single best thing to happen to me in my career was having had Kellan placed in charge of me. I stuck around long enough to see Kellan’s technical decisionmaking start to bear fruit. I learned a great deal from this, but I also learned a great deal as a result of this. I would not have been free to become the engineer that wrote Data Driven Products Now! if Kellan had not been there to so thoroughly stick the landing on technology choices.

In the year since leaving Etsy, I’ve resurrected my ability to care about technology. And my thoughts have crystallized to the point where I can write them down coherently. What follows is a distillation of the Kellan gestalt, which will hopefully serve to horrify him only slightly.

Embrace Boredom.

Let’s say every company gets about three innovation tokens. You can spend these however you want, but the supply is fixed for a long while. You might get a few more after you achieve a certain level of stability and maturity, but the general tendency is to overestimate the contents of your wallet. Clearly this model is approximate, but I think it helps.

If you choose to write your website in NodeJS, you just spent one of your innovation tokens. If you choose to use MongoDB, you just spent one of your innovation tokens. If you choose to use service discovery tech that’s existed for a year or less, you just spent one of your innovation tokens. If you choose to write your own database, oh god, you’re in trouble.

Any of those choices might be sensible if you’re a javascript consultancy, or a database company. But you’re probably not. You’re probably working for a company that is at least ostensibly rethinking global commerce or reinventing payments on the web or pursuing some other suitably epic mission. In that context, devoting any of your limited attention to innovating ssh is an excellent way to fail. Or at best, delay success [1].

What counts as boring? That’s a little tricky. “Boring” should not be conflated with “bad.” There is technology out there that is both boring and bad [2]. You should not use any of that. But there are many choices of technology that are boring and good, or at least good enough. MySQL is boring. Postgres is boring. PHP is boring. Python is boring. Memcached is boring. Squid is boring. Cron is boring.

The nice thing about boringness (so constrained) is that the capabilities of these things are well understood. But more importantly, their failure modes are well understood. Anyone who knows me well will understand that it’s only with a overwhelming sense of malaise that I now invoke the spectre of Don Rumsfeld, but I must.

When choosing technology, you have both known unknowns and unknown unknowns [3].

  • A known unknown is something like: we don’t know what happens when this database hits 100% CPU.
  • An unknown unknown is something like: geez it didn’t even occur to us that writing stats would cause GC pauses.

Both sets are typically non-empty, even for tech that’s existed for decades. But for shiny new technology the magnitude of unknown unknowns is significantly larger, and this is important.

Optimize Globally.

I unapologetically think a bias in favor of boring technology is a good thing, but it’s not the only factor that needs to be considered. Technology choices don’t happen in isolation. They have a scope that touches your entire team, organization, and the system that emerges from the sum total of your choices.

Adding technology to your company comes with a cost. As an abstract statement this is obvious: if we’re already using Ruby, adding Python to the mix doesn’t feel sensible because the resulting complexity would outweigh Python’s marginal utility. But somehow when we’re talking about Python and Scala or MySQL and Redis people lose their minds, discard all constraints, and start raving about using the best tool for the job.

Your function in a nutshell is to map business problems onto a solution space that involves choices of software. If the choices of software were truly without baggage, you could indeed pick a whole mess of locally-the-best tools for your assortment of problems.

But of course, the baggage exists. We call the baggage “operations” and to a lesser extent “cognitive overhead.” You have to monitor the thing. You have to figure out unit tests. You need to know the first thing about it to hack on it. You need an init script. I could go on for days here, and all of this adds up fast.

The problem with “best tool for the job” thinking is that it takes a myopic view of the words “best” and “job.” Your job is keeping the company in business, god damn it. And the “best” tool is the one that occupies the “least worst” position for as many of your problems as possible.

It is basically always the case that the long-term costs of keeping a system working reliably vastly exceed any inconveniences you encounter while building it. Mature and productive developers understand this.

Choose New Technology, Sometimes.

Taking this reasoning to its reductio ad absurdum would mean picking Java, and then trying to implement a website without using anything else at all. And that would be crazy. You need some means to add things to your toolbox.

An important first step is to acknowledge that this is a process, and a conversation. New tech eventually has company-wide effects, so adding tech is a decision that requires company-wide visibility. Your organizational specifics may force the conversation, or they may facilitate developers adding new databases and queues without talking to anyone. One way or another you have to set cultural expectations that this is something we all talk about.

One of the most worthwhile exercises I recommend here is to consider how you would solve your immediate problem without adding anything new. First, posing this question should detect the situation where the “problem” is that someone really wants to use the technology. If that is the case, you should immediately abort.

It can be amazing how far a small set of technology choices can go. The answer to this question in practice is almost never “we can’t do it,” it’s usually just somewhere on the spectrum of “well, we could do it, but it would be too hard” [4]. If you think you can’t accomplish your goals with what you’ve got now, you are probably just not thinking creatively enough.

It’s helpful to write down exactly what it is about the current stack that makes solving the problem prohibitively expensive and difficult. This is related to the previous exercise, but it’s subtly different.

New technology choices might be purely additive (for example: “we don’t have caching yet, so let’s add memcached”). But they might also overlap or replace things you are already using. If that’s the case, you should set clear expectations about migrating old functionality to the new system. The policy should typically be “we’re committed to migrating,” with a proposed timeline. The intention of this step is to keep wreckage at manageable levels, and to avoid proliferating locally-optimal solutions.

This process is not daunting, and it’s not much of a hassle. It’s a handful of questions to fill out as homework, followed by a meeting to talk about it. I think that if a new technology (or a new service to be created on your infrastructure) can pass through this gauntlet unscathed, adding it is fine.

Just Ship.

Polyglot programming is sold with the promise that letting developers choose their own tools with complete freedom will make them more effective at solving problems. This is a naive definition of the problems at best, and motivated reasoning at worst. The weight of day-to-day operational toil this creates crushes you to death.

Mindful choice of technology gives engineering minds real freedom: the freedom to contemplate bigger questions. Technology for its own sake is snake oil.

Update, July 27th 2015: I wrote a talk based on this article. You can see it here.

  1. Etsy in its early years suffered from this pretty badly. We hired a bunch of Python programmers and decided that we needed to find something for them to do in Python, and the only thing that came to mind was creating a pointless middle layer that required years of effort to amputate. Meanwhile, the 90th percentile search latency was about two minutes. Etsy didn't fail, but it went several years without shipping anything at all. So it took longer to succeed than it needed to.
  2. We often casually refer to the boring/bad intersection of doom as “enterprise software,” but that terminology may be imprecise.
  3. In saying this Rumsfeld was either intentionally or unintentionally alluding to the Socratic Paradox. Socrates was by all accounts a thoughtful individual in a number of ways that Rumsfeld is not.

  4. A good example of this from my experience is Etsy’s activity feeds. When we built this feature, we were working pretty hard to consolidate most of Etsy onto PHP, MySQL, Memcached, and Gearman (a PHP job server). It was much more complicated to implement the feature on that stack than it might have been with something like Redis (or maybe not). But it is absolutely possible to build activity feeds on that stack.

    An amazing thing happened with that project: our attention turned elsewhere for several years. During that time, activity feeds scaled up 20x while nobody was watching it at all. We made no changes whatsoever specifically targeted at activity feeds, but everything worked out fine as usage exploded because we were using a shared platform. This is the long-term benefit of restraint in technology choices in a nutshell.

    This isn’t an absolutist position--while activity feeds stored in memcached was judged to be practical, implementing full text search with faceting in raw PHP wasn't. So Etsy used Solr.

blocks.html_en: I unapologetically think a bias in favor of boring technology is a good thing, but it’s not the only factor that needs to be considered. Technology choices don’t happen in isolation. They have a scope that touches your entire team, organization, and the system that emerges from the sum total of your choices.

sentences.en: I unapologetically think a bias in favor of boring technology is a good thing, but it’s not the only factor that needs to be considered.
sentences.zh: 我毫无歉意地认为偏爱无聊技术是一件好事，但这并不是唯一需要考虑的因素。

sentences.en: Technology choices don’t happen in isolation.
sentences.zh: 技术选择并不是孤立发生的。

sentences.en: They have a scope that touches your entire team, organization, and the system that emerges from the sum total of your choices.
sentences.zh: 它们的范围涉及您的整个团队、组织以及从您的选择总和中产生的系统。

blocks.html_en: Adding technology to your company comes with a cost. As an abstract statement this is obvious: if we’re already using Ruby, adding Python to the mix doesn’t feel sensible because the resulting complexity would outweigh Python’s marginal utility. But somehow when we’re talking about Python and Scala or MySQL and Redis people lose their minds, discard all constraints, and start raving about using the best tool for the job.

sentences.en: Adding technology to your company comes with a cost.
sentences.zh: 为您的公司添加技术是需要付出成本的。

sentences.en: As an abstract statement this is obvious: if we’re already using Ruby, adding Python to the mix doesn’t feel sensible because the resulting complexity would outweigh Python’s marginal utility.
sentences.zh: 作为一个抽象的陈述，这是显而易见的：如果我们已经在使用 Ruby，那么将 Python 添加到混合中并不明智，因为由此产生的复杂性将超过 Python 的边际效用。

sentences.en: But somehow when we’re talking about Python and Scala or MySQL and Redis people lose their minds, discard all constraints, and start raving about using the best tool for the job.
sentences.zh: 但不知何故，当我们谈论 Python 和 Scala 或 MySQL 和 Redis 时，人们会失去理智，抛弃所有限制，并开始热衷于使用最好的工具来完成工作。

blocks.html_en: Your function in a nutshell is to map business problems onto a solution space that involves choices of software. If the choices of software were truly without baggage, you could indeed pick a whole mess of locally-the-best tools for your assortment of problems.

sentences.en: Your function in a nutshell is to map business problems onto a solution space that involves choices of software.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，您的职责是将业务问题映射到涉及软件选择的解决方案空间。

sentences.en: If the choices of software were truly without baggage, you could indeed pick a whole mess of locally-the-best tools for your assortment of problems.
sentences.zh: 如果软件的选择确实没有负担，那么您确实可以选择一大堆本地最好的工具来解决您的各种问题。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>The way you might choose technology in a world where choices are cheap: "pick the right tool for the job."</figcaption>

sentences.en: The way you might choose technology in a world where choices are cheap: "pick the right tool for the job."
sentences.zh: 在一个选择成本低廉的世界中，您选择技术的方式是：“为工作选择正确的工具。”

blocks.html_en: But of course, the baggage exists. We call the baggage “operations” and to a lesser extent “cognitive overhead.” You have to monitor the thing. You have to figure out unit tests. You need to know the first thing about it to hack on it. You need an init script. I could go on for days here, and all of this adds up fast.

sentences.en: But of course, the baggage exists.
sentences.zh: 但当然，行李是存在的。

sentences.en: We call the baggage “operations” and to a lesser extent “cognitive overhead.”
sentences.zh: 我们将这些包袱称为“操作”，并在较小程度上称为“认知开销”。

sentences.en: You have to monitor the thing.
sentences.zh: 你必须监视这件事。

sentences.en: You have to figure out unit tests.
sentences.zh: 你必须弄清楚单元测试。

sentences.en: You need to know the first thing about it to hack on it.
sentences.zh: 你需要首先了解它才能破解它。

sentences.en: You need an init script.
sentences.zh: 您需要一个初始化脚本。

sentences.en: I could go on for days here, and all of this adds up fast.
sentences.zh: 我可以在这里待上几天，所有这些加起来很快。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>The way you choose technology in the world where operations are a serious concern (i.e., "reality"). </figcaption>

sentences.en: The way you choose technology in the world where operations are a serious concern (i.e., "reality").
sentences.zh: 在运营受到严重关注的世界（即“现实”）中，您选择技术的方式。

blocks.html_en: The problem with “best tool for the job” thinking is that it takes a myopic view of the words “best” and “job.” Your job is keeping the company in business, god damn it. And the “best” tool is the one that occupies the “least worst” position for as many of your problems as possible.

sentences.en: The problem with “best tool for the job” thinking is that it takes a myopic view of the words “best” and “job.”
sentences.zh: “工作的最佳工具”思维的问题在于，它对“最佳”和“工作”这两个词采取了短视的看法。

sentences.en: Your job is keeping the company in business, god damn it.
sentences.zh: 你的工作就是维持公司的运转，该死的。

sentences.en: And the “best” tool is the one that occupies the “least worst” position for as many of your problems as possible.
sentences.zh: “最好”的工具是对尽可能多的问题占据“最不最糟糕”位置的工具。

blocks.html_en: It is basically always the case that the long-term costs of keeping a system working reliably vastly exceed any inconveniences you encounter while building it. Mature and productive developers understand this.

sentences.en: It is basically always the case that the long-term costs of keeping a system working reliably vastly exceed any inconveniences you encounter while building it.
sentences.zh: 基本上总是这样，保持系统可靠运行的长期成本远远超过构建系统时遇到的任何不便。

sentences.en: Mature and productive developers understand this.
sentences.zh: 成熟且高效的开发人员都明白这一点。

blocks.html_en: Choose New Technology, Sometimes.

sentences.en: Choose New Technology, Sometimes.
sentences.zh: 有时选择新技术。

blocks.html_en: Taking this reasoning to its reductio ad absurdum would mean picking Java, and then trying to implement a website without using anything else at all. And that would be crazy. You need some means to add things to your toolbox.

sentences.en: Taking this reasoning to its reductio ad absurdum would mean picking Java, and then trying to implement a website without using anything else at all.
sentences.zh: 将此推理归结为荒谬，意味着选择 Java，然后尝试在不使用其他任何东西的情况下实现一个网站。

sentences.en: And that would be crazy.
sentences.zh: 那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: You need some means to add things to your toolbox.
sentences.zh: 您需要一些方法来将东西添加到您的工具箱中。

blocks.html_en: An important first step is to acknowledge that this is a process, and a conversation. New tech eventually has company-wide effects, so adding tech is a decision that requires company-wide visibility. Your organizational specifics may force the conversation, or they may facilitate developers adding new databases and queues without talking to anyone. One way or another you have to set cultural expectations that this is something we all talk about.

sentences.en: An important first step is to acknowledge that this is a process, and a conversation.
sentences.zh: 重要的第一步是承认这是一个过程，也是一次对话。

sentences.en: New tech eventually has company-wide effects, so adding tech is a decision that requires company-wide visibility.
sentences.zh: 新技术最终会对全公司产生影响，因此添加技术是一个需要全公司可见性的决定。

sentences.en: Your organizational specifics may force the conversation, or they may facilitate developers adding new databases and queues without talking to anyone.
sentences.zh: 您的组织细节可能会迫使对话，或者它们可能会帮助开发人员在不与任何人交谈的情况下添加新的数据库和队列。

sentences.en: One way or another you have to set cultural expectations that this is something we all talk about.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，你必须设定文化期望，这是我们都在谈论的事情。

blocks.html_en: One of the most worthwhile exercises I recommend here is to consider how you would solve your immediate problem without adding anything new. First, posing this question should detect the situation where the “problem” is that someone really wants to use the technology. If that is the case, you should immediately abort.

sentences.en: One of the most worthwhile exercises I recommend here is to consider how you would solve your immediate problem without adding anything new.
sentences.zh: 我在这里推荐的最有价值的练习之一是考虑如何在不添加任何新内容的情况下解决当前的问题。

sentences.en: First, posing this question should detect the situation where the “problem” is that someone really wants to use the technology.
sentences.zh: 首先，提出这个问题应该找出“问题”是有人真的想使用该技术的情况。

sentences.en: If that is the case, you should immediately abort.
sentences.zh: 如果是这种情况，您应该立即中止。

blocks.html_en: <figcaption>I just watched a webinar about this graph database, we should try it out.</figcaption>

sentences.en: I just watched a webinar about this graph database, we should try it out.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚观看了有关此图数据库的网络研讨会，我们应该尝试一下。

blocks.html_en: It can be amazing how far a small set of technology choices can go. The answer to this question in practice is almost never “we can’t do it,” it’s usually just somewhere on the spectrum of “well, we could do it, but it would be too hard” [4]. If you think you can’t accomplish your goals with what you’ve got now, you are probably just not thinking creatively enough.

sentences.en: It can be amazing how far a small set of technology choices can go.
sentences.zh: 一小部分技术选择可以走多远，真是令人惊奇。

sentences.en: The answer to this question in practice is almost never “we can’t do it,” it’s usually just somewhere on the spectrum of “well, we could do it, but it would be too hard” [4].
sentences.zh: 在实践中，这个问题的答案几乎从来都不是“我们做不到”，它通常只是“好吧，我们可以做到，但太难了”[4]。

sentences.en: If you think you can’t accomplish your goals with what you’ve got now, you are probably just not thinking creatively enough.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为用现在的能力无法实现你的目标，那么你可能只是没有足够的创造性思维。

blocks.html_en: It’s helpful to write down exactly what it is about the current stack that makes solving the problem prohibitively expensive and difficult. This is related to the previous exercise, but it’s subtly different.

sentences.en: It’s helpful to write down exactly what it is about the current stack that makes solving the problem prohibitively expensive and difficult.
sentences.zh: 准确地写下当前堆栈的哪些内容使得解决问题变得异常昂贵和困难是有帮助的。

sentences.en: This is related to the previous exercise, but it’s subtly different.
sentences.zh: 这与之前的练习相关，但略有不同。

blocks.html_en: New technology choices might be purely additive (for example: “we don’t have caching yet, so let’s add memcached”). But they might also overlap or replace things you are already using. If that’s the case, you should set clear expectations about migrating old functionality to the new system. The policy should typically be “we’re committed to migrating,” with a proposed timeline. The intention of this step is to keep wreckage at manageable levels, and to avoid proliferating locally-optimal solutions.

sentences.en: New technology choices might be purely additive (for example: “we don’t have caching yet, so let’s add memcached”).
sentences.zh: 新技术选择可能纯粹是附加的（例如：“我们还没有缓存，所以让我们添加 memcached”）。

sentences.en: But they might also overlap or replace things you are already using.
sentences.zh: 但它们也可能会重叠或取代您已经在使用的东西。

sentences.en: If that’s the case, you should set clear expectations about migrating old functionality to the new system.
sentences.zh: 如果是这种情况，您应该对将旧功能迁移到新系统设定明确的期望。

sentences.en: The policy should typically be “we’re committed to migrating,” with a proposed timeline.
sentences.zh: 该政策通常应该是“我们致力于迁移”，并附有拟议的时间表。

sentences.en: The intention of this step is to keep wreckage at manageable levels, and to avoid proliferating locally-optimal solutions.
sentences.zh: 此步骤的目的是将残骸保持在可管理的水平，并避免局部最优解决方案激增。

blocks.html_en: This process is not daunting, and it’s not much of a hassle. It’s a handful of questions to fill out as homework, followed by a meeting to talk about it. I think that if a new technology (or a new service to be created on your infrastructure) can pass through this gauntlet unscathed, adding it is fine.

sentences.en: This process is not daunting, and it’s not much of a hassle.
sentences.zh: 这个过程并不令人畏惧，也没有太大的麻烦。

sentences.en: It’s a handful of questions to fill out as homework, followed by a meeting to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 需要填写一些问题作为家庭作业，然后开会讨论。

sentences.en: I think that if a new technology (or a new service to be created on your infrastructure) can pass through this gauntlet unscathed, adding it is fine.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果一项新技术（或在您的基础设施上创建的新服务）能够毫发无伤地通过这个考验，那么添加它就可以了。

blocks.html_en: Just Ship.

sentences.en: Just Ship.
sentences.zh: 就船吧。

blocks.html_en: Polyglot programming is sold with the promise that letting developers choose their own tools with complete freedom will make them more effective at solving problems. This is a naive definition of the problems at best, and motivated reasoning at worst. The weight of day-to-day operational toil this creates crushes you to death.

sentences.en: Polyglot programming is sold with the promise that letting developers choose their own tools with complete freedom will make them more effective at solving problems.
sentences.zh: 多语言编程的销售承诺是让开发人员完全自由地选择自己的工具将使他们更有效地解决问题。

sentences.en: This is a naive definition of the problems at best, and motivated reasoning at worst.
sentences.zh: 这往好了说是对问题的天真定义，往坏了说是有动机的推理。

sentences.en: The weight of day-to-day operational toil this creates crushes you to death.
sentences.zh: 由此产生的日常运营工作的重担会把你压垮。

blocks.html_en: Mindful choice of technology gives engineering minds real freedom: the freedom to contemplate bigger questions. Technology for its own sake is snake oil.

sentences.en: Mindful choice of technology gives engineering minds real freedom: the freedom to contemplate bigger questions.
sentences.zh: 谨慎的技术选择为工程师的思维提供了真正的自由：思考更大问题的自由。

sentences.en: Technology for its own sake is snake oil.
sentences.zh: 技术本身就是万金油。

blocks.html_en: Update, July 27th 2015: I wrote a talk based on this article. You can see it here.

sentences.en: Update, July 27th 2015: I wrote a talk based on this article.
sentences.zh: 2015 年 7 月 27 日更新：我根据这篇文章写了一篇演讲。

sentences.en: You can see it here.
sentences.zh: 你可以在这里看到它。

blocks.html_en: • Etsy in its early years suffered from this pretty badly. We hired a bunch of Python programmers and decided that we needed to find something for them to do in Python, and the only thing that came to mind was creating a pointless middle layer that required years of effort to amputate. Meanwhile, the 90th percentile search latency was about two minutes. Etsy didn't fail, but it went several years without shipping anything at all. So it took longer to succeed than it needed to.

sentences.en: Etsy in its early years suffered from this pretty badly.
sentences.zh: Etsy 在成立之初就深受其害。

sentences.en: We hired a bunch of Python programmers and decided that we needed to find something for them to do in Python, and the only thing that came to mind was creating a pointless middle layer that required years of effort to amputate.
sentences.zh: 我们雇佣了一群 Python 程序员，并决定需要为他们在 Python 中找到一些东西，而唯一想到的就是创建一个毫无意义的中间层，需要多年的努力才能被截除。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the 90th percentile search latency was about two minutes.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，第 90 个百分点的搜索延迟约为两分钟。

sentences.en: Etsy didn't fail, but it went several years without shipping anything at all.
sentences.zh: Etsy 并没有失败，但它已经好几年没有发布任何东西了。

sentences.en: So it took longer to succeed than it needed to.
sentences.zh: 因此，取得成功所需的时间比所需的时间更长。

blocks.html_en: • We often casually refer to the boring/bad intersection of doom as “enterprise software,” but that terminology may be imprecise.

sentences.en: We often casually refer to the boring/bad intersection of doom as “enterprise software,” but that terminology may be imprecise.
sentences.zh: 我们经常随意地将这种无聊/糟糕的厄运交集称为“企业软件”，但这个术语可能不准确。

blocks.html_en: • In saying this Rumsfeld was either intentionally or unintentionally alluding to the Socratic Paradox. Socrates was by all accounts a thoughtful individual in a number of ways that Rumsfeld is not.

sentences.en: In saying this Rumsfeld was either intentionally or unintentionally alluding to the Socratic Paradox.
sentences.zh: 拉姆斯菲尔德说这句话时有意无意地暗指苏格拉底悖论。

sentences.en: Socrates was by all accounts a thoughtful individual in a number of ways that Rumsfeld is not.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，苏格拉底在很多方面都是一个有思想的人，而拉姆斯菲尔德则不然。

blocks.html_en:
• A good example of this from my experience is Etsy’s activity feeds. When we built this feature, we were working pretty hard to consolidate most of Etsy onto PHP, MySQL, Memcached, and Gearman (a PHP job server). It was much more complicated to implement the feature on that stack than it might have been with something like Redis (or maybe not). But it is absolutely possible to build activity feeds on that stack.

    An amazing thing happened with that project: our attention turned elsewhere for several years. During that time, activity feeds scaled up 20x while nobody was watching it at all. We made no changes whatsoever specifically targeted at activity feeds, but everything worked out fine as usage exploded because we were using a shared platform. This is the long-term benefit of restraint in technology choices in a nutshell.

    This isn’t an absolutist position--while activity feeds stored in memcached was judged to be practical, implementing full text search with faceting in raw PHP wasn't. So Etsy used Solr.

sentences.en: A good example of this from my experience is Etsy’s activity feeds.
sentences.zh: 根据我的经验，Etsy 的活动提要就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: When we built this feature, we were working pretty hard to consolidate most of Etsy onto PHP, MySQL, Memcached, and Gearman (a PHP job server).
sentences.zh: 当我们构建此功能时，我们非常努力地将大部分 Etsy 整合到 PHP、MySQL、Memcached 和 Gearman（一个 PHP 作业服务器）上。

sentences.en: It was much more complicated to implement the feature on that stack than it might have been with something like Redis (or maybe not).
sentences.zh: 在该堆栈上实现该功能比使用 Redis（或者可能不是）之类的东西要复杂得多。

sentences.en: But it is absolutely possible to build activity feeds on that stack.
sentences.zh: 但绝对有可能在该堆栈上构建活动源。

sentences.en: An amazing thing happened with that project: our attention turned elsewhere for several years.
sentences.zh: 这个项目发生了一件令人惊奇的事情：几年来我们的注意力转向了其他地方。

sentences.en: During that time, activity feeds scaled up 20x while nobody was watching it at all.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，活动源的规模扩大了 20 倍，而根本没有人在观看。

sentences.en: We made no changes whatsoever specifically targeted at activity feeds, but everything worked out fine as usage exploded because we were using a shared platform.
sentences.zh: 我们没有专门针对活动提要进行任何更改，但一切都很顺利，因为我们使用的是共享平台，所以使用量激增。

sentences.en: This is the long-term benefit of restraint in technology choices in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这就是限制技术选择的长期好处。

sentences.en: This isn’t an absolutist position--while activity feeds stored in memcached was judged to be practical, implementing full text search with faceting in raw PHP wasn't.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一个绝对主义的立场——虽然存储在 memcached 中的活动提要被认为是实用的，但在原始 PHP 中使用分面实现全文搜索则不然。

sentences.en: So Etsy used Solr.
sentences.zh: 因此 Etsy 使用了 Solr。

content_html_zh:
也许在我的职业生涯中发生在我身上的最好的事情就是让凯兰来负责我。 我坚持了足够长的时间，看到凯兰的技术决策开始取得成果。 我从中学到了很多东西，但我也因此学到了很多东西。 我现在就无法自由地成为编写数据驱动产品的工程师！ 如果凯兰没有在那里如此彻底地坚持技术选择的着陆。

离开 Etsy 后的一年里，我恢复了关心技术的能力。 我的想法已经具体化到可以连贯地写下来的程度。 接下来是凯兰格式塔的精炼，希望这只会让他感到轻微的恐惧。

拥抱无聊。

假设每家公司都获得大约三个创新代币。 你可以随心所欲地花这些钱，但供应量在很长一段时间内是固定的。 当你达到一定程度的稳定性和成熟度后，你可能会得到更多，但总体趋势是高估你钱包的内容。 显然这个模型是近似的，但我认为它有帮助。

如果您选择用 NodeJS 编写网站，您只需花费一枚创新代币。 如果您选择使用 MongoDB，您只需花费一枚创新代币。 如果您选择使用已经存在一年或更短时间的服务发现技术，您只需花费一个创新代币。 如果你选择编写自己的数据库，天哪，你就有麻烦了。

如果您是一家 JavaScript 咨询公司或一家数据库公司，那么这些选择中的任何一个都可能是明智的。 但你可能不是。 您所工作的公司可能至少在表面上正在重新思考全球商业或重新发明网络支付或追求其他一些适当的史诗般的使命。 在这种情况下，将有限的注意力投入到 ssh 创新上将会导致失败。 或者充其量只是延迟成功[1]。

什么才算无聊？ 这有点棘手。 “无聊”不应该与“糟糕”混为一谈。 有些技术既无聊又糟糕 [2]。 你不应该使用其中任何一个。 但有很多技术选择虽然无聊，但也很好，或者至少足够好。 MySQL 很无聊。 Postgres 很无聊。 PHP 很无聊。 Python 很无聊。 Memcached 很无聊。 鱿鱼很无聊。 克朗很无聊。

无聊（如此受限）的好处是这些东西的功能可以很好地理解。 但更重要的是，它们的故障模式是众所周知的。 任何熟悉我的人都会明白，我现在只是怀着一种压倒性的不适感才会唤起唐·拉姆斯菲尔德的幽灵，但我必须这样做。

在选择技术时，你既有已知的未知数，也有未知的未知数[3]。

  • 已知的未知是这样的：我们不知道当这个数据库达到 100% CPU 时会发生什么。
  • 未知的未知就像这样：天哪，我们甚至没有想到写入统计数据会导致 GC 暂停。

即使对于已经存在了几十年的技术来​​说，这两个集合通常都是非空的。 但对于闪亮的新技术来说，未知的未知数要大得多，这一点很重要。

全局优化。

我毫无歉意地认为偏爱无聊技术是一件好事，但这并不是唯一需要考虑的因素。 技术选择并不是孤立发生的。 它们的范围涉及您的整个团队、组织以及从您的选择总和中产生的系统。

为您的公司添加技术是需要付出成本的。 作为一个抽象的陈述，这是显而易见的：如果我们已经在使用 Ruby，那么将 Python 添加到混合中并不明智，因为由此产生的复杂性将超过 Python 的边际效用。 但不知何故，当我们谈论 Python 和 Scala 或 MySQL 和 Redis 时，人们会失去理智，抛弃所有限制，并开始热衷于使用最好的工具来完成工作。

简而言之，您的职责是将业务问题映射到涉及软件选择的解决方案空间。 如果软件的选择确实没有负担，那么您确实可以选择一大堆本地最好的工具来解决您的各种问题。

但当然，行李是存在的。 我们将这些包袱称为“操作”，并在较小程度上称为“认知开销”。 你必须监视这件事。 你必须弄清楚单元测试。 你需要首先了解它才能破解它。 您需要一个初始化脚本。 我可以在这里待上几天，所有这些加起来很快。

“工作的最佳工具”思维的问题在于，它对“最佳”和“工作”这两个词采取了短视的看法。 你的工作就是维持公司的运转，该死的。 “最好”的工具是对尽可能多的问题占据“最不最糟糕”位置的工具。

基本上总是这样，保持系统可靠运行的长期成本远远超过构建系统时遇到的任何不便。 成熟且高效的开发人员都明白这一点。

有时选择新技术。

将此推理归结为荒谬，意味着选择 Java，然后尝试在不使用其他任何东西的情况下实现一个网站。 那太疯狂了。 您需要一些方法来将东西添加到您的工具箱中。

重要的第一步是承认这是一个过程，也是一次对话。 新技术最终会对全公司产生影响，因此添加技术是一个需要全公司可见性的决定。 您的组织细节可能会迫使对话，或者它们可能会帮助开发人员在不与任何人交谈的情况下添加新的数据库和队列。 不管怎样，你必须设定文化期望，这是我们都在谈论的事情。

我在这里推荐的最有价值的练习之一是考虑如何在不添加任何新内容的情况下解决当前的问题。 首先，提出这个问题应该找出“问题”是有人真的想使用该技术的情况。 如果是这种情况，您应该立即中止。

一小部分技术选择可以走多远，真是令人惊奇。 在实践中，这个问题的答案几乎从来都不是“我们做不到”，它通常只是“好吧，我们可以做到，但太难了”[4]。 如果你认为用现在的能力无法实现你的目标，那么你可能只是没有足够的创造性思维。

准确地写下当前堆栈的哪些内容使得解决问题变得异常昂贵和困难是有帮助的。 这与之前的练习相关，但略有不同。

新技术选择可能纯粹是附加的（例如：“我们还没有缓存，所以让我们添加 memcached”）。 但它们也可能会重叠或取代您已经在使用的东西。 如果是这种情况，您应该对将旧功能迁移到新系统设定明确的期望。 该政策通常应该是“我们致力于迁移”，并附有拟议的时间表。 此步骤的目的是将残骸保持在可管理的水平，并避免局部最优解决方案激增。

这个过程并不令人畏惧，也没有太大的麻烦。 需要填写一些问题作为家庭作业，然后开会讨论。 我认为，如果一项新技术（或在您的基础设施上创建的新服务）能够毫发无伤地通过这个考验，那么添加它就可以了。

就船吧。

多语言编程的销售承诺是让开发人员完全自由地选择自己的工具将使他们更有效地解决问题。 这往好了说是对问题的天真定义，往坏了说是有动机的推理。 由此产生的日常运营工作的重担会把你压垮。

谨慎的技术选择为工程师的思维提供了真正的自由：思考更大问题的自由。 技术本身就是万金油。

2015 年 7 月 27 日更新：我根据这篇文章写了一篇演讲。 你可以在这里看到它。

  1. Etsy 在成立之初就深受其害。 我们雇佣了一群 Python 程序员，并决定需要为他们在 Python 中找到一些东西，而唯一想到的就是创建一个毫无意义的中间层，需要多年的努力才能被截除。 与此同时，第 90 个百分点的搜索延迟约为两分钟。 Etsy 并没有失败，但它已经好几年没有发布任何东西了。 因此，取得成功所需的时间比所需的时间更长。
  2. 我们经常随意地将这种无聊/糟糕的厄运交集称为“企业软件”，但这个术语可能不准确。
  3. 拉姆斯菲尔德说这句话时有意无意地暗指苏格拉底悖论。 众所周知，苏格拉底在很多方面都是一个有思想的人，而拉姆斯菲尔德则不然。
  4. 根据我的经验，Etsy 的活动提要就是一个很好的例子。 当我们构建此功能时，我们非常努力地将大部分 Etsy 整合到 PHP、MySQL、Memcached 和 Gearman（一个 PHP 作业服务器）上。 在该堆栈上实现该功能比使用 Redis（或者可能不是）之类的东西要复杂得多。 但绝对有可能在该堆栈上构建活动源。 这个项目发生了一件令人惊奇的事情：几年来我们的注意力转向了其他地方。 在那段时间里，活动源的规模扩大了 20 倍，而根本没有人在观看。 我们没有专门针对活动提要进行任何更改，但一切都很顺利，因为我们使用的是共享平台，所以使用量激增。 简而言之，这就是限制技术选择的长期好处。 这并不是一个绝对主义的立场——虽然存储在 memcached 中的活动提要被认为是实用的，但在原始 PHP 中使用分面实现全文搜索则不然。 因此 Etsy 使用了 Solr。
